shortcut_name: candidate graph is necessarily a tree
evidence: deepseek: "Remove non-essential leaves"; gpt-oss: "# = n-1"; all solutions build an undirected adjacency list and exploit unique tree paths
affordance_in_statement: The given candidate conduits provide a fully integrated blueprint: using all candidate conduits, it is possible to travel between any two stations, and there are exactly n − 1 candidate conduits in total.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal under the immutable constraints: connectedness together with exactly n − 1 undirected conduits intrinsically makes the input a tree. Defeating this shortcut would require allowing cyclic candidate networks or otherwise changing the task.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Peels non-essential leaves until only the minimal subtree containing essential stations remains, then sums its edges.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The candidate conduits form a connected graph with exactly n − 1 edges, so leaf pruning is valid.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses tree traversal and sums the unique paths or the edges in the essential-containing subtree.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement explicitly guarantees a connected n-vertex graph with m = n − 1.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Builds an adjacency list and computes the minimal subtree connecting the marked stations rather than solving general Steiner connectivity.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The blueprint is a connected graph with exactly n − 1 candidate conduits.

common_affordance: The candidate network is an undirected tree, so every pair of stations has a unique path and the answer is the sum of edges in the minimal subtree spanning the essential stations.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its union-find/Kruskal-style approach treats the instance as a generic spanning-tree or MST selection problem and does not correctly isolate the unique minimal subtree connecting only the essential stations.

recommended_edit: No legal edit can defeat all survivors while preserving the immutable input constraints and task: the tree structure is forced mathematically. If those constraints may be relaxed, allow candidate networks with cycles (m greater than n − 1) while retaining the same connectivity objective.
